option_a_derivation.units_axes: The outer viewBox is '0 0 width graphHeight' in CSS px (width = the svg's getBoundingClientRect width = column), so outer a is close to 1 and dimensionless. Camera screen CTM = outer_a * (naturalScale*scale) and node-0 screen size = outer_a * camera; dividing by outer_a gives viewBox units. a==d and b==c==0 make the division valid on both axes; translations are irrelevant to sizes
option_a_derivation.expected_height: JS graphHeight = H32*naturalScale*min(1, 520/(W32*naturalScale)) = H32*min(naturalScale, 520/W32), the binary32 image of Python expected*height. After the 300px resize the guard W0*natural0 <= 300 keeps fitWidth = 1, so natural0*H0 is correct; the worker's 120x80 fixture violates that guard and was correctly special-cased in its validator only
option_a_derivation.outer_bounds: Under truncation H_L = floor(f32(gH)*k)/k with vbh = f32(gH), so vbh - H_L lies in [0, 1/k) with k=64 at DPR 1. Hence |H_L - expected| <= 1/64 + |f32(gH) - expected|, |vbh - expected| <= representation, meet = min(W/vw, H/vh), and (1-a)*vbh = vbh - H_L <= 1/64 (CSS px). The combined allowance on raw camera values equals R3's Option B propagated term, plus structural checks. Normalization therefore cannot absorb more than one layout unit
option_a_derivation.gamma5: Higham gamma_n bound for products/quotients of n relative roundings. Branches: A-branch H32*Aw/W32 (W's parse rounding cancels; H32 + pt->px conversion = 2, or 3 if the 4/3 constant is float), 450/W32 and fit branches 2, 300/H32 branch 0; then +1 for the viewBox read and +1 for a float screen matrix gives <= 5. Binary64 noise (~1e-15) is far below gamma5 - 5u ~ 25u^2. Observed in Chromium: CSS length = f32(gH) (812.40624 -> 812.40625 snapped), a = H/vh exactly in double, so the matrix term is unused. The view_height check used <= 0.358 of representation in all engine samples
option_a_derivation.residual_limits: Parser: gamma5 is rigorous only for correctly rounded parsing. Chromium parsed correctly in every observed case (24/24 viewBox reads equal f32 of the JS shortest repr; the model reproduces 9/9 worker and 15/15 own values), so digit-accumulation excess is modeled only; WebKit is unknown. Tall: see R4-N3 (executed)
